subject.title: PR1/5 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this residual cross-owner durable-core RFC as the canonical architecture direction alongside the existing TaskFlow and background-task owners?
rationale: The documents intentionally define future cross-owner invariants and are the stated foundation for a large dependent runtime stack; source review can verify consistency but cannot authorize that repository-level architecture direction.

options.title: Sponsor one residual-gap RFC
options.body: Fix the glossary, explicitly enumerate which invariants are not already owned by TaskFlow and tasks, and make this the sole canonical proposal.

options.title: Fold into current owner docs
options.body: Move any accepted residual requirements into the existing TaskFlow and background-task architecture pages instead of creating a parallel durable-core concept.

options.title: Pause the durable-core stack
options.body: Leave this and dependent implementation work unmerged until maintainers agree that a new shared layer is needed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor one residual-gap RFC
recommendation.body: Fix the glossary, explicitly enumerate which invariants are not already owned by TaskFlow and tasks, and make this the sole canonical proposal.

likelyOwner.reason: The TaskFlow substrate commit is the clearest established ownership boundary for the durable flow, persistence, and operator semantics discussed here.
